acerca.ante: What Nyango is and who made each part
acerca.que.p1: Nyango teaches Kaishi 1.5k (vocabulary and kanji) and grammar, with its own guide, with spaced repetition, with Nyan as your companion. It's free, runs on your computer, and never sends anything online on its own.
acerca.que.p2: Each lesson goes from small to big: first the elements (the pieces kanji are drawn with), then the kanji, and then the words that use them. It assumes you can already read hiragana and katakana: if not, start with those two lessons in Grammar {g}.
acerca.anki.cuerpo: It never touches your cards. If you turn on syncing, it saves a _nyango file in your Anki media folder, and AnkiWeb carries it to your other computers.
acerca.kaishi.cuerpo: Nyango is not affiliated with or endorsed by {kaishi} or its authors. Its text doesn't come inside the app: each installation generates it from your own Anki the first time you start it.
acerca.radicales.cuerpo: The elements deck is {nemui}'s, also generated from your Anki.
acerca.media.cuerpo: The audio (NHK, JLPT Tango) and the irasutoya images are served from your local Anki. Nyango never redistributes them or stores them in the package.
acerca.gramatica.cuerpo: Written for Nyango: the explanations, examples and exercises are original.
acerca.kanjium.cuerpo: Reading and kanji data from Kanjium and KANJIDIC2/EDRDG — CC BY-SA 4.0.
acerca.voces.cuerpo: Nyan's voice (his little noises and the sentences) and the audio of NyanDeck, our own deck, are made with {voicevox}: VOICEVOX:ずんだもん (Nyan), VOICEVOX:四国めたん (the words), VOICEVOX:猫使ビィ (Tama), VOICEVOX:猫使アル (Kage), VOICEVOX:玄野武宏 (Pon), VOICEVOX:冥鳴ひまり (Fukuro), VOICEVOX:白上虎太郎 (Kotarō) and VOICEVOX:九州そら (the storyteller).
acerca.motor.cuerpo: {three} (MIT) and {gsap} (standard no-charge license). Fonts under the OFL.
arranque.sin_anki.p: Nyango doesn't ship Kaishi 1.5k inside the app: for licensing reasons, it reads it from your own Anki collection, only on this computer.
arranque.faltan_mazos.tit: A couple of decks are missing
arranque.faltan_mazos.p: I found Anki, but not the Kaishi 1.5k deck or its elements deck.
arranque.paso2: Download {kaishi}: on the latest release page, the file that ends in .apkg.
arranque.paso3: Also download the {radicales} deck (the elements of Kaishi 1.5k) from its AnkiWeb page.
arranque.paso4: Open them in Anki with File → Import so they're saved in your collection, then come back here.

clase.frase.intro: Tap the pieces to build the sentence. The room will do exactly what you say… to the letter.
clase.frase.primero: Tell me what's there and where. The place takes に and the thing takes が.
clase.frase.siguiente_encargo: Another task! Look at the picture.
clase.frase.otra_vez: Come on, again. Look at the task picture.
clase.msg.ok: That's it! Exactly what I asked for. にゃー！
clase.msg.orden: That works too! You changed the order, but the particles say the same thing.
clase.msg.vida: Whoa! With いる, {algo} came alive. いる is for things that move on their own; for objects, ある.
clase.msg.peluche: With ある, {algo} went stiff like a plushie. For things that move on their own: いる.
clase.msg.al_reves: You put {algo} on top of {sitio}! に marks the PLACE and が what's there.
clase.msg.otro: Well said… but that's not what I asked for. Again!
clase.msg.vida_ok: The apple is alive! Sounds like a horror story, but you said it perfectly.
clase.msg.vida_casi: With ある the apple just sits there. Which verb wakes it up?
clase.juego.intro: Does it move by itself? いる. No? ある. Quick!
clase.juego.nyan: I show you something and you send it to its basket. Careful, there are traps.
clase.juego.fin: {bien} of {total}. Not bad! I got confused by the tree.
clase.juego.perfecto: {bien} of {total}! Not a single miss. I'd have got the cat wrong.

clase.apuntes.reg_txt: です and ます are the polite form: with the teacher, in shops, with older people or strangers. With friends and family, like Tama, you talk casually and drop them: 大[おお]きいですね → 大[おお]きいね, 行[い]きます → 行[い]く. It isn't rude: it's closeness.

ajustes.bv.nota: The welcome asks about your level again and makes you a new plan. The tour just shows you the home screen.
bv.saludo.p: I want to learn Japanese, but I can't do it on my own. Here's a deal: you learn, and then you teach me. That way we both learn. Deal?
bv.nombre.p: So I know who to thank every day. Your name or a nickname.
bv.motivo.tit: Why do you want to learn Japanese?
bv.motivo.p: Pick as many as you like. That way I know what to tell you.
bv.tiempo.tit: How much time do you have a day?
bv.tiempo.p: What counts most is not skipping a day, even if it's just a little while.
bv.nivel.tit: How much Japanese do you know?
bv.nivel.basico_d: Greetings and single words · roughly N5
bv.nivel.medio_d: Simple sentences, a few hundred kanji · N4
bv.prueba.p: To find where to start: a few kana and a few words. If you don't know something, press «I don't know». That's fine, and it helps me get your level right.
bv.plan.p_cero: First the letters (the kana), then words and grammar. I'll be with you all the way.
bv.plan.tit_kana: You can read: on to the words!
bv.plan.p_kana: You start with the first words on the road, the most common ones in Japanese.
bv.plan.p_n: I'm placing you in region {region} of the road, from word {n}. The ones you know I'll ask you bit by bit over the coming months, to check.
bv.rec.kana: **Learn the kana** in the «Kana» section: one column a day and in a couple of weeks you'll read hiragana.
bv.rec.katakana: **Brush up your katakana** in «Kana»: you'll need it for words like ケーキ (cake).
bv.rec.rutina.5: **Your 5-minute routine**: the daily review. A new lesson whenever you have spare time.
bv.rec.rutina.10: **Your 10-minute routine**: the review and a five-word lesson.
bv.rec.rutina.20: **Your 20-minute routine**: review, a lesson and, a couple of times a week, a grammar class.
bv.rec.rutina.30: **Your 30-minute routine**: review, lesson, a grammar class and, for dessert, a story.
bv.rec.clase: **Grammar classes** are episodes with Tama, Kage and the others. Yours is: «{clase}».
bv.rec.clase_primera: **Grammar classes** are episodes with Tama, Kage and the others. Start with the first one once you know hiragana.
bv.rec.motivo.anime: **For anime**: «Stories» has short tales with audio, and the classes use street Japanese, not textbook Japanese.
bv.rec.motivo.viajar: **For the trip**: look out for the shop, street and train classes; those are the phrases you'll use there.
bv.rec.motivo.juegos: **For games**: each region of the road ends with a yōkai. Beat it with what you've learned.
bv.rec.motivo.amigos: **For talking to people**: the classes show when to speak casually (with Tama) and when to use です and ます.
bv.rec.motivo.jlpt: **For the JLPT**: words go by frequency, so N5 and N4 come first. «Your Japanese» shows how far you've got.
bv.rec.motivo.trabajo: **For work or studies**: consistency beats marathons. The daily review is what counts most.
bv.rec.motivo.cultura: **For the culture**: the classes visit festivals, shrines and a winter in Hokkaido. Check each one's notes.
bv.rec.repaso: **Don't skip the review**: even one minute keeps your streak alive. If you can't one day, a charm protects it.

bv.nyan.motivo.trabajo: How serious… I'd better put on a tie.

bv.nyan.plan: Here's your plan, {nombre}! What do you think?
tour.repaso: Every day I ask you the cards that are due, just before you'd forget them. **It's the most important thing**: a few minutes, but every day.
tour.leccion: New words, five at a time, with their kanji. First you see them, then I test you.
tour.gramatica: Classes that are episodes: Tama, Kage and the others live a story and each class teaches one point. Plus a guide to read.
tour.kanji: The map of every kanji: the ones you know light up. Tap one to see its strokes and its words.
tour.camino: The whole journey: regions of fifty words and, at the end of each, **a yōkai** to beat with what you've learned.
tour.historias: Short tales with audio you can read with what you know. They open up as you progress.
tour.mochi: What you win (clothes, furniture, decorations) goes here. And here you see everything you've taught me.
tour.kana: Hiragana and katakana: how each one is written, how it sounds and a game to practise them.
tour.carta: Whatever you pick below shows up here, with what's next and **the button to start**. Arrow keys and Enter work too.
tour.misiones: Three missions a day. With the koban you earn you buy things in the shop, and lucky bags bring surprises.
tour.estadisticas: Your numbers: how much you know, your streak and, above all, **your next step**.
tour.ajustes: Sound, review mode, language, your progress backup… and here you can see this welcome again.
bv.plan.p_todo: You know the whole road! I'll ask you bit by bit over the coming months, to check, and all the classes and stories are yours.
bv.rec.clase_salta: **Grammar classes** go from the most basic to the most advanced. At your level, skim the notes of the first ones and carry on where you fall short.
acerca.kanjivg.cuerpo: The stroke order and shapes of hiragana and katakana come from {kanjivg}, by Ulrich Apel, licensed CC BY-SA 3.0. The kana mnemonics and audio are Nyango's own.
clase.indice.f_pronto: This class is still being made. It's coming soon, with Nyan, Tama and the others!
acerca.que.p1_app: Nyango teaches you Japanese from scratch: the kana, 3,000 words with their kanji, grammar through classes that are little episodes plus a reference guide, and spaced reviews so you don't forget anything. With Nyan as your companion. It's free, works offline and never sends anything online on its own.
acerca.que.p2_app: Each lesson goes from small to big: first the elements (the pieces kanji are drawn with), then the kanji, and then the words that use them. If you can't read hiragana and katakana yet, start with the «Kana» section.
acerca.nyandeck.cuerpo: Nyango's own deck: the word list and its order, the example sentences, the mnemonics, the classes and the stories are Nyango's.
acerca.fotos.cuerpo: The scenes are photos from {unsplash}, used under its licence. Their authors are listed in the CREDITOS.md file.
ep.final.guia: To study this in more depth, see {lecciones} in the grammar guide.
